acceptanceCriteria: A shared bound/limit helper (or documented contract) in internal/contextindex makes bound exhaustion return a typed unresolved reason that callers must propagate to ALL/uncertainty.
A table-driven test drives every analyzer bound (depth, hop, nesting, template depth, source size) one past its limit and asserts no `selected`/certain result.
A negative-cache rule: in-progress recursion markers are never stored as permanent negative results (regression test with an export cycle).
Spec requirement recorded in the governing contextindex/TSA spec.
body: Recurring class across reviews: PR #1096 Codex (2026-10-18) found 7 P1 fail-opens in internal/contextindex/setup_shared.go (re-export hop bound, template depth bound, cycle marker cached as negative, export * as, require/dynamic import, namespace values, declaring-module reads); PR #1088 Codex found an unenforced Ruby nesting bound; V1-1478 and V1-1717 track similar JS/TS registry fail-opens. Each analyzer hand-rolls its bounds, and hitting one returns the same result as a genuine negative. This breaks product invariant 2 (missing evidence yields uncertainty, never invented certainty). Related: V1-1478, V1-1717.
title: contextindex analyzers need one fail-closed bound contract: every exhausted bound or unsupported form must emit an unresolved reason, never a silent selected
